title: Candidate isolation in Neptune
summary: A separate named graph alone is not quarantine in Neptune.

sections.label: Verified behavior
sections.text: Neptune’s default SPARQL graph is the union of named graphs. An unscoped serving query can therefore encounter candidate assertions.

sections.label: Design options
sections.text: Use a separate candidate store/environment, or enforce and test explicit approved datasets throughout serving queries. Audit every relevant serving path rather than assuming a candidate graph label prevents exposure.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: Candidate-only assertions do not appear through ordinary REST/UI serving before the approved publication process. Include a regression scenario for this boundary.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow use: Architecture and impact, Tests and review, Release and production. Use when designing candidate-data isolation, testing serving paths and reviewing a proposed promotion into an approved serving dataset. This is an Atlas recommendation reviewed on 2026-10-15, not a mandatory process or an observed execution result.
Check output to obtain: Record the actual candidate and approved dataset boundaries, every relevant serving query and the proposed promotion owner.
Check output to obtain: Insert a candidate-only fixture in a permitted test environment and verify it is absent from each ordinary serving path.
Check output to obtain: Record promotion and reversal evidence under the actual release process. A named-graph label alone is not an isolation test.

basis: Documented engine behavior + required design check

catalog.applicability: Use this when candidate assertions are stored in a Neptune named graph next to approved data and serving queries use SPARQL. The default graph is the union of named graphs, so use a separate candidate store or enforce explicit approved datasets and audit every serving path.
